message.reasoning:
I'm reviewing my position in this Monopoly game—I've got $991 in cash and control the light-blue properties with 4 houses each. The bank is out of houses but still has 10 hotels available, so I could upgrade to hotels and free up those houses, though my opponents are nearly broke with only around $100-140 each.

The key insight is that keeping my 12 houses locked up maintains a house shortage that prevents GPT from developing his green and yellow properties further—he's stuck at 2-3 houses on several of them. If I build hotels and return those houses to the bank, I'd actually help him develop, which defeats my strategy. My rent is already devastating to everyone, so the best move is to hold steady and end my turn without making any changes.
